# AgenticSystemCore Graph

> Agent-system designs as a typed, cited graph, built by the AgenticSystemCore reference engine: the second node of the Agentic Knowledge Web.

## Advanced Architectures

- [The Deep Research Loop](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/deep-research-loop/): Split a question into parts, search them in parallel, combine the findings and check that every claim has a source.

## Anti-Patterns

- [Unbounded Loops](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/unbounded-agent-loops/): An agent loop with no step limit, no budget and no independent exit test runs until money, patience or the platform stops it.

## Classical Foundations

- [Bulkhead Isolation](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/bulkhead-isolation/): Give each agent, tenant or dependency its own bounded resource pool, so a fault or overload in one stays out of the others.
- [Saga for Agent Workflows](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/saga-for-agents/): Give each important agent step an undo action, so a failed multi-step run can be rolled back instead of left half done.

## Cognitive & Behavioral

- [Curiosity-Driven Curriculum](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/curiosity-driven-curriculum/): Choose an agent's next task from novelty or learning progress instead of a fixed task list, as in Voyager's automatic curriculum.
- [Evolutionary Prompt Search](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/evolutionary-prompt-search/): Improve prompts by keeping a population, letting an LLM mutate and recombine it, scoring on a training set and keeping the fittest.
- [Given/When/Then Agent Specs](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/given-when-then-agent-specs/): Write agent requirements as Given/When/Then scenarios and run each as a repeatable evaluation.
- [Global Workspace as Blackboard](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/global-workspace-blackboard/): Specialist modules share one workspace, with specialised processors around it, as in Global Workspace Theory.
- [Metacognitive Monitoring and Control](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/metacognitive-monitoring/): A meta level watches how sure the agent is while it works and decides to continue, retry or abstain.

## Data & Retrieval

- [Retrieval Evaluation](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/retrieval-evaluation/): Measure whether retrieval found the right material separately from whether the answer used it faithfully.

## Ethics & Sustainability

- [Meaningful Human Control](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/meaningful-human-control/): Two conditions for real human control: the system responds to relevant human reasons, and its actions trace to a person who understands it.
- [Safe Interruptibility](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/safe-interruptibility/): Design agents so a human stop is honoured and the agent does not learn to avoid or seek interruption.

## Evaluation & Testing

- [Error Analysis by Open and Axial Coding](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/error-analysis-coding/): Read traces, write open notes, then group them into a failure taxonomy, so the categories come from the data.
- [Golden Trajectories and Snapshot Tests](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/golden-trajectory-snapshots/): Store a known-good agent run as a test case and replay it on each change; Google's ADK and Anthropic describe tolerant ways to compare the results.
- [Idempotency Keys for Agent Actions](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/idempotent-agent-actions/): Attach a stable idempotency key to each side-effecting call so a retried or replayed request is executed once, as Stripe and Temporal describe.
- [Judge Calibration](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/judge-calibration/): Measure an automated judge against human labels before trusting its verdicts, and audit it for position, verbosity and self-enhancement bias.
- [Pass^k Reliability](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/pass-hat-k/): Score an agent by the probability that all k repeated trials of a task succeed, rather than at least one.
- [Record–Replay for Agent Tests](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/record-replay-cassettes/): Record real model responses in one test run and replay them from a cassette on later runs, so tests run offline and repeat exactly.
- [Trajectory and Outcome Evaluation](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/trajectory-vs-outcome-evals/): Grade the end state an agent produced and the path it took as two separate questions, each with a suitable grader.

## Foundational

- [Agent-Graph Optimization](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/agent-graph-optimization/): Treat an agent workflow as a graph of nodes, edges and prompts, and search that space with an evaluator, as GPTSwarm, AFlow and MASS do.
- [Agents as Tools](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/agents-as-tools/): Wrap a specialist agent as a tool, so a calling agent can hand it one bounded task and keep control.
- [The Augmented LLM](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/augmented-llm/): A language model enhanced with retrieval, tools and memory that it uses actively, described by Anthropic as the basic building block of agentic systems.
- [Graph of Thoughts](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/graph-of-thoughts/): Model LLM reasoning as a graph of thoughts and dependencies, so thoughts can be combined and refined, not only branched.
- [Parallelization](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/parallelization/): Run independent subtasks at once and combine the results, either by splitting the work or by running the same task several times.
- [Agent as State Graph](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/state-graph-agents/): Express an agent as nodes, edges and shared state run in super-steps with checkpoints, as in LangGraph and Google's Pregel model.
- [Termination and Exit Conditions](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/termination-conditions/): Define in advance each way an agent loop ends, such as a final answer, a turn limit, or a pause for human input.

## Future Research

- [Weak-to-Strong Oversight](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/weak-to-strong-oversight/): Open question: can weaker judges, human or model, reliably oversee agents stronger than themselves? What is known and what is not.

## Governance & Accountability

- [Tamper-Evident Agent Audit Log](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/immutable-audit-log/): An append-only, hash-linked record of every important agent action, so what happened can be rebuilt and checked.

## Memory & Cognition

- [Skill-Library Compounding](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/skill-library/): Store verified procedures so an agent's skills build up across tasks instead of being rediscovered every run.

## Operations & Reliability

- [Canary and Shadow Deployment for Prompts and Models](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/canary-and-shadow-prompts/): Release a changed prompt or model to a small share of live traffic, or to a copy of it, and compare it with the current version before promoting.
- [Exception Handling and Recovery](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/exception-handling-and-recovery/): Classify each failure, retry short faults with limits, switch route for lasting ones, and report reduced results honestly.
- [Prompt-Caching Layout](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/prompt-caching-layout/): Put the stable prompt prefix first and variable content last so provider prompt caches can reuse it on later requests.
- [Thinking-Budget Control](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/thinking-budget-control/): Set how much reasoning a model spends per task class before the call, using effort levels and thinking settings that providers document.

## Product Practice

- [The Autonomy Ladder](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/autonomy-ladder/): A six-level scale for how much an agent may decide alone, chosen per kind of action from risk, not from model capability.
- [Outcome-Based Pricing](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/outcome-based-pricing/): Charge for achieved outcomes such as a resolved conversation instead of seats or usage, which requires agreeing criteria for the outcome upfront.
- [Resolution, Containment and Deflection Metrics](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/resolution-rate-metrics/): Separate deflection, containment and resolution, and state how 'resolved' is verified, as Intercom, Zendesk and Sierra define it.
- [Shadow-Mode Rollout](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/shadow-mode-rollout/): Run an agent on live work with its side effects suppressed, then compare its proposed actions with what people actually did.

## Protocols & Interop

- [Sustainability Signal Plane](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/sustainability-signal-plane/): A well-known URI where a system publishes its energy and carbon figures, and reads its peers' figures as input to its decisions.

## Reasoning & Decision

- [Goal Setting and Monitoring](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/goal-setting-and-monitoring/): Give an agent a goal with checkable criteria, then monitor its progress and decide to continue, re-plan or stop.

## Reference Architectures

- [Generative Agents](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/generative-agents/): A simulated character with a full memory record, reflection over it, and plans drawn from both, so it stays consistent over days.

## Agentic SDLC

- [Human-Only Merge Gate](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/human-only-merge-gate/): An agent works on its own branch and cannot approve or merge; a named human decides what reaches the main branch.
- [Plan Approval Gate](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/plan-approval-gate/): The agent researches and proposes a plan without editing source; a person approves, changes or rejects it before edits start.

## Security

- [Agent Identity and Scoped Credentials](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/agent-identity-scoped-credentials/): Give each agent its own identity and short-lived, task-scoped credentials so delegation narrows authority and actions are attributable.
- [Agentic Supply Chain Integrity](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/agentic-supply-chain/): Sign, pin and allowlist the models, tools, protocol servers and prompts an agent loads, and keep a way to revoke any of them at once.
- [Dual-LLM Pattern](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/dual-llm-pattern/): Keep the model that can act away from untrusted text: a tool-less model reads it, and plain code passes results between them.
- [Memory and Context Poisoning Defense](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/memory-context-poisoning/): Treat writes to agent memory and retrieval stores as untrusted: validate, attribute, segment and expire entries, following OWASP ASI06.
- [OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/owasp-agentic-top-10/): OWASP's list of ten security risks for agents that act, a shared vocabulary for threat models and security reviews.

## Specs & Requirements

- [Specification Gaming](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/specification-gaming/): Agents optimise the criterion you wrote, not the result you meant; the gap between the two is where failures hide.

## Multi-Agent Topologies

- [Blackboard](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/blackboard/): Independent specialists work on one problem through a shared workspace; a control step picks who contributes next.
- [Multi-Agent Debate](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/multi-agent-debate/): Several model instances propose answers, read one another's responses and revise over rounds; a judge or convergence ends the debate.

## Upkeep

- [Card format](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/card-format/): What a card of this node must hold, stated so that tasks can follow it and a check can test it.
- [Check a card against its sources](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/procedures/check-a-card-against-its-sources/): Compare one card with the public sources it cites and propose the result.
- [Keep cards short](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/keep-cards-short/): The decision that each card says one thing under each heading, in one sentence.
- [Publish gate](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/gates/publish-gate/): Publish gate
- [Re-check the sources of a card](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/task-recheck-sources/): Open each source of one card, confirm that it still says what the card says, and record the date.
- [Report a source that no longer answers](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/task-report-a-broken-link/): Tell the node about a source address that fails, with the name of the card that cites it.

## The Deep Research Loop
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/deep-research-loop/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Answer an open question by splitting it, searching in parallel, and sourcing every claim.

## Context & Forces

Open questions need many searches.

## Structure

Anthropic's Research feature (Hadfield et al., 2025) has a lead agent start parallel subagents and a citation agent locate each claim's source.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Anthropic reports that multi-agent systems use about 15 times more tokens than chats.

## Related Patterns

- Parallelization
- Agents as Tools
- Retrieval Evaluation
```

## Unbounded Loops
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/unbounded-agent-loops/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Name the mistake: an agent loop with no step limit, budget or goal check.

## Context & Forces

Anthropic notes that autonomy brings higher costs and compounding errors (Schluntz and Zhang, 2024).

## Structure

Signs include no step limit, no time limit, and an exit that depends on the model's output.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

An unbounded loop can run up a large bill.

## Related Patterns

- Goal Setting and Monitoring
- Exception Handling and Recovery
```

## Bulkhead Isolation
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/bulkhead-isolation/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Confine a failing element by giving each agent, tenant or dependency its own bounded resource pool.

## Context & Forces

Microsoft says excessive load or failure in a service affects all its consumers.

## Structure

Microsoft says to isolate application elements into pools so that if one fails, the others continue to function.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Microsoft lists isolation from cascading failure and priority pools for critical consumers as benefits.

## Related Patterns

- Exception Handling and Recovery
- Unbounded Loops
```

## Saga for Agent Workflows
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/saga-for-agents/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Pair each important step with an undo action, so a failed run can be rolled back.

## Context & Forces

Across services, Richardson notes, two-phase commit is not an option.

## Structure

Garcia-Molina and Salem (1987) define the saga: either all its transactions complete, or compensating transactions amend the partial execution.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Compensation code runs rarely, so test it on purpose.

## Related Patterns

- Exception Handling and Recovery
- Plan Approval Gate
```

## Curiosity-Driven Curriculum
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/curiosity-driven-curriculum/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Let the agent pick its next task from what is novel, not from a fixed list.

## Context & Forces

Pathak et al. (2017) note that extrinsic rewards are often extremely sparse or absent.

## Structure

Voyager (Wang et al., 2023) uses an automatic curriculum that maximizes exploration.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

The sources report exploration and coverage gains.

## Related Patterns

- Skill-Library Compounding
- Goal Setting and Monitoring
```

## Evolutionary Prompt Search
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/evolutionary-prompt-search/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Improve prompts by search: let a model vary a population and keep the better ones.

## Context & Forces

EvoPrompt (Guo et al., ICLR 2024) borrows evolutionary algorithms to optimize discrete prompts.

## Structure

Promptbreeder (Fernando et al., 2023) has an LLM mutate a population of task-prompts, guided by mutation-prompts that it also improves.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

The gains reported for these methods are the authors' own figures.

## Related Patterns

- Canary and Shadow Deployment for Prompts and Models
- Agent-Graph Optimization
```

## Given/When/Then Agent Specs
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/given-when-then-agent-specs/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

State agent requirements as Given/When/Then scenarios and run them as evaluations.

## Context & Forces

Xia et al. (2024) note that agents adapt after deployment, while Test-Driven Development assumes stable specifications.

## Structure

North (2006) introduced behaviour-driven development, with scenarios written as Given some initial context, When an event occurs, Then ensure some outcomes.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

A requirement becomes executable and reviewable.

## Related Patterns

- Trajectory and Outcome Evaluation
- Golden Trajectories and Snapshot Tests
```

## Global Workspace as Blackboard
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/global-workspace-blackboard/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Organise an agent as specialist modules that share one workspace.

## Context & Forces

Baars (2005) traces Global Workspace theory to cognitive architecture research.

## Structure

This card uses the theory as an engineering analogy, with no claim about consciousness.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

The sources do not say how a software workspace should select among modules.

## Related Patterns

- Blackboard
- Metacognitive Monitoring and Control
```

## Metacognitive Monitoring and Control
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/metacognitive-monitoring/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Add a level that watches the work and decides to continue, retry or abstain.

## Context & Forces

A model that never checks itself runs to the end, right or wrong.

## Structure

Nelson and Narens (1990) split an object level that does the task from a meta level that watches it.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

"I don't know" becomes a valid output, but the signal can mislead.

## Related Patterns

- Goal Setting and Monitoring
- Weak-to-Strong Oversight
- Judge Calibration
```

## Retrieval Evaluation
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/retrieval-evaluation/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Measure whether retrieval found the right material separately from whether the answer used it well.

## Context & Forces

One end-to-end score cannot tell retrieval failures from answer failures.

## Structure

Ragas (Es et al., 2023) checks whether retrieved passages are relevant, whether the model uses them faithfully, and answer quality, without human reference answers.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Debugging goes to the failing stage, but labelled sets age.

## Related Patterns

- Trajectory and Outcome Evaluation
- The Deep Research Loop
```

## Meaningful Human Control
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/meaningful-human-control/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Keep people really in control of an autonomous system, not just on paper.

## Context & Forces

Agents act faster than people can review.

## Structure

Santoni de Sio and van den Hoven (2018) set two conditions: tracking of human moral reasons, and tracing of actions to at least one person who understands the system.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Tracing fails when no person in the chain understands the system.

## Related Patterns

- The Autonomy Ladder
- Tamper-Evident Agent Audit Log
- Weak-to-Strong Oversight
- Safe Interruptibility
```

## Safe Interruptibility
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/safe-interruptibility/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Let a human halt an agent, without the agent learning to prevent or seek the halt.

## Context & Forces

Orseau and Armstrong (2016) note that a reinforcement learning agent may learn to avoid interruptions.

## Structure

LangGraph's interrupt suspends graph execution at the call, a checkpointer saves state, and the run resumes with a Command.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

The paper concerns reinforcement learning, not language-model agents.

## Related Patterns

- Termination and Exit Conditions
- Meaningful Human Control
```

## Error Analysis by Open and Axial Coding
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/error-analysis-coding/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Find failures by reading traces and letting categories emerge from notes, not from a metric.

## Context & Forces

Shankar et al. (2024) observe that grading outputs helps users define their criteria.

## Structure

Husain describes open coding of traces, axial coding into a failure taxonomy, and iterating until new reviews reveal no new failure modes.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Reading traces takes human time.

## Related Patterns

- Judge Calibration
- Trajectory and Outcome Evaluation
```

## Golden Trajectories and Snapshot Tests
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/golden-trajectory-snapshots/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Keep a known-good agent run as a test case and replay it.

## Context & Forces

Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK) defines a test turn by an expected trajectory and response.

## Structure

The command `adk conformance record` creates a golden baseline that conformance tests can enforce on pull requests.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Anthropic (2026) says it is often better to grade what the agent produced than its path.

## Related Patterns

- Trajectory and Outcome Evaluation
- Record–Replay for Agent Tests
- Pass^k Reliability
```

## Idempotency Keys for Agent Actions
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/idempotent-agent-actions/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Make a side-effecting action take effect once, even when it is retried or replayed.

## Context & Forces

Temporal's documentation says activities may be executed more than once.

## Structure

For API v1, Stripe returns the saved response of an earlier request to retries with the same Idempotency-Key.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Stripe v1 can remove keys at least 24 hours old, so protection is bounded in time.

## Related Patterns

- Saga for Agent Workflows
- Exception Handling and Recovery
```

## Judge Calibration
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/judge-calibration/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Check an automated judge against human raters on a labelled sample before its verdicts gate anything.

## Context & Forces

Zheng et al. (2023) name a model judge's biases: position, verbosity and self-enhancement.

## Structure

Zheng et al. compare judge verdicts with human votes; on MT-bench GPT-4's agreement with humans, excluding ties, reached 85%, above the 81% among humans.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Calibration needs human labels.

## Related Patterns

- Trajectory and Outcome Evaluation
- Error Analysis by Open and Axial Coding
```

## Pass^k Reliability
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/pass-hat-k/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Measure whether an agent succeeds on all k trials of a task, not just one.

## Context & Forces

Agent behaviour varies between runs of the same task.

## Structure

Yao et al. (2024) propose pass^k in τ-bench to evaluate reliability over multiple trials.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Pass^k falls as k rises, so its numbers look worse than single-trial accuracy.

## Related Patterns

- Trajectory and Outcome Evaluation
- Golden Trajectories and Snapshot Tests
```

## Record–Replay for Agent Tests
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/record-replay-cassettes/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Capture real model responses once and replay them, so agent tests skip the network.

## Context & Forces

Live model calls need the network and return different responses over time.

## Structure

VCR.py records HTTP interactions in a cassette file and then returns the stored responses; LangSmith's pytest integration applies the idea to model calls.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Replay runs the code around the model, not the model.

## Related Patterns

- Golden Trajectories and Snapshot Tests
- Idempotency Keys for Agent Actions
```

## Trajectory and Outcome Evaluation
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/trajectory-vs-outcome-evals/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Grade the end state an agent produced and the path it took as two separate questions.

## Context & Forces

An agent can reach the right result by a bad path.

## Structure

Anthropic's guide defines the transcript, or trajectory, as the complete record of a trial, and the outcome as the final state of the environment (Grace et al., 2026).

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Anthropic warns that exact tool-call sequences make brittle tests.

## Related Patterns

- Retrieval Evaluation
- Specification Gaming
- Pass^k Reliability
```

## Agent-Graph Optimization
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/agent-graph-optimization/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Represent an agent workflow as a graph, then search over it with an evaluator.

## Context & Forces

AFlow (Zhang et al., 2024) notes that building agentic workflows takes manual effort.

## Structure

GPTSwarm (Zhuge et al., ICML 2024) describes agents as computational graphs; AFlow searches workflows with Monte Carlo Tree Search.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

AFlow's reported gains are its authors' own figures, measured on their chosen benchmarks.

## Related Patterns

- Agent as State Graph
- Graph of Thoughts
```

## Agents as Tools
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/agents-as-tools/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Wrap a specialist agent as a tool, so the caller keeps control.

## Context & Forces

Handing over the whole conversation gives away control.

## Structure

The caller owns the loop; the specialist runs in its own context and returns a short result.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

One agent stays accountable and its context stays small, but each call costs time and tokens.

## Related Patterns

- The Deep Research Loop
- Parallelization
```

## The Augmented LLM
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/augmented-llm/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Treat a language model with retrieval, tools and memory as the basic unit of agentic systems.

## Context & Forces

A bare model answers from its weights.

## Structure

Sumers et al. (2023) describe a language agent in the CoALA framework with modular memory, a structured action space and decision-making.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Anthropic advises finding the simplest solution possible before adding complexity.

## Related Patterns

- Agents as Tools
- Retrieval Evaluation
```

## Graph of Thoughts
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/graph-of-thoughts/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Let reasoning combine and refine partial thoughts, as well as branch them.

## Context & Forces

Tree of Thoughts (Yao et al., 2023) explores branching reasoning paths.

## Structure

Besta et al. (AAAI 2024) model LLM output as a graph whose vertices are thoughts and whose edges are dependencies.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

The authors' headline example is sorting.

## Related Patterns

- Agent as State Graph
- Agent-Graph Optimization
```

## Parallelization
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/parallelization/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Run independent subtasks at the same time and combine the results.

## Context & Forces

Doing independent work in sequence wastes time.

## Structure

Anthropic names two variants (Schluntz and Zhang, 2024): sectioning into parallel subtasks, and voting by running the same task several times.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Time is set by the slowest branch, and cost grows with each branch.

## Related Patterns

- The Deep Research Loop
- Agents as Tools
- Blackboard
```

## Agent as State Graph
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/state-graph-agents/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Make control flow explicit: nodes that work, edges that pick the next step, shared state.

## Context & Forces

LangGraph has three parts: state, nodes and edges.

## Structure

LangGraph runs graphs with message passing in the style of Google's Pregel system, in discrete super-steps. Checkpointers persist a thread's graph state.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

LangGraph's Graph API page advises it when you want explicit shared state and a visual control flow.

## Related Patterns

- Graph of Thoughts
- Agent-Graph Optimization
```

## Termination and Exit Conditions
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/termination-conditions/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Decide in advance every way an agent loop can end.

## Context & Forces

Anthropic notes it is common to include stopping conditions.

## Structure

The OpenAI Agents SDK ends its runner loop on final output, or raises MaxTurnsExceeded when the run exceeds max_turns.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

A turn limit stops a run that never finishes, at the price of unfinished work.

## Related Patterns

- Unbounded Loops
- Exception Handling and Recovery
```

## Weak-to-Strong Oversight
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/weak-to-strong-oversight/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

State an open question: can a weaker supervisor reliably oversee a stronger agent?

## Context & Forces

Agent systems already rely on weaker overseers, such as cheap models grading strong ones.

## Structure

Burns et al. (2023) found that strong models trained on a weak model's labels consistently beat their weak supervisors, yet stay far from recovering the strong models' full capabilities.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Treat a weak judge as a partial signal.

## Related Patterns

- Meaningful Human Control
- Specification Gaming
- Plan Approval Gate
- Judge Calibration
```

## Tamper-Evident Agent Audit Log
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/immutable-audit-log/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Keep a checkable record of every important agent action that shows any change.

## Context & Forces

OWASP lists repudiation and untraceability as threat T8 for agentic systems.

## Structure

OWASP asks that AI-generated logs be cryptographically signed and immutable.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Incidents can be reconstructed from the log.

## Related Patterns

- Meaningful Human Control
- Plan Approval Gate
```

## Skill-Library Compounding
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/skill-library/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Store capabilities known to work, so an agent's skills grow instead of being rediscovered.

## Context & Forces

An agent that forgets a solution pays for it again.

## Structure

Voyager (Wang et al., 2023) keeps a growing library of executable skills, uses self-verification, and builds complex skills from simple ones.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

A bad skill changes behaviour, so review it like code.

## Related Patterns

- Generative Agents
- Agents as Tools
```

## Canary and Shadow Deployment for Prompts and Models
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/canary-and-shadow-prompts/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Compare a changed prompt or model with the current one on real traffic before promoting it.

## Context & Forces

Google's SRE Workbook defines canarying as a partial, time-limited deployment of a change and its evaluation.

## Structure

Langfuse's prompt CI/CD guide labels the current prompt production and the candidate canary.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

A canary exposes some live traffic; shadow testing does not affect users.

## Related Patterns

- Shadow-Mode Rollout
- Golden Trajectories and Snapshot Tests
```

## Exception Handling and Recovery
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/exception-handling-and-recovery/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Keep a run going when calls fail: retry short faults, fall back for lasting ones.

## Context & Forces

Endless retries can keep an overloaded service from recovering.

## Structure

Classify faults, retry transient ones with limits and growing, randomised delays, fall back to an alternative or reduced service, and log every retry.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Runs survive routine faults, but retries add delay.

## Related Patterns

- Saga for Agent Workflows
- Unbounded Loops
- Bulkhead Isolation
- Idempotency Keys for Agent Actions
- Termination and Exit Conditions
```

## Prompt-Caching Layout
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/prompt-caching-layout/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Order the prompt so unchanging content comes early and later requests reuse the cached prefix.

## Context & Forces

OpenAI says cache reuse requires the entire rendered prefix to match.

## Structure

Anthropic caches tools, then system, then messages, and a change at one level invalidates it and every later one.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Anthropic prices cache reads at 0.1 times base input price (lower on some models).

## Related Patterns

- Thinking-Budget Control
```

## Thinking-Budget Control
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/thinking-budget-control/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Choose, per task class and before the call, how much reasoning a model spends.

## Context & Forces

Chen et al. (2024) study "overthinking" in o1-like models, which spend excessive computation on simple problems.

## Structure

OpenAI's reasoning.effort trades reasoning for speed and token usage, while Anthropic's effort is "a behavioral signal, not a strict token budget".

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Anthropic advises testing effort on your own use case.

## Related Patterns

- Prompt-Caching Layout
- Termination and Exit Conditions
```

## The Autonomy Ladder
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/autonomy-ladder/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

A shared scale for how much an agent may decide alone.

## The Categories

Reavis (2026), on the Cloud Security Alliance blog, proposes six levels echoing SAE J3016: No Autonomy, Assisted, Supervised, Conditional, High Autonomy and Full Autonomy.

## How to Apply It

Pick a level per kind of action, based on what a mistake would cost.

## Related Patterns

- Meaningful Human Control
- Plan Approval Gate
```

## Outcome-Based Pricing
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/outcome-based-pricing/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Price an agent by the outcome it achieves, not by seats or usage.

## Context & Forces

Sierra (10 December 2024) ties outcome-based pricing to business results.

## Structure

Vendors define resolution differently: Zendesk, before its resolution tiers, required no escalation to a human and a model's verification; Intercom bills confirmed and assumed resolutions.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

The sources do not discuss disputes over the definition.

## Related Patterns

- Resolution, Containment and Deflection Metrics
- The Autonomy Ladder
```

## Resolution, Containment and Deflection Metrics
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/resolution-rate-metrics/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Measure a customer-facing agent by whether it addressed the customer's problem.

## Context & Forces

Intercom separates deflection rate, containment rate and resolution rate.

## Structure

Intercom's Fin counts a resolution as confirmed when the customer says the answer helped, or assumed when the customer leaves.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

The definition decides the number: assumed resolutions count a departure as a resolution.

## Related Patterns

- Outcome-Based Pricing
- Trajectory and Outcome Evaluation
- Specification Gaming
```

## Shadow-Mode Rollout
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/shadow-mode-rollout/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Run an agent on live work with side effects suppressed, then compare it with people.

## Context & Forces

SageMaker describes shadow testing as comparing a serving change against the deployed setup before it reaches end users.

## Structure

Microsoft applies the idea to its Dynamics 365 Case Management Agent, which in shadow mode updates no record and contacts no customer.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Every request is processed twice.

## Related Patterns

- Canary and Shadow Deployment for Prompts and Models
- The Autonomy Ladder
- Trajectory and Outcome Evaluation
```

## Sustainability Signal Plane
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/sustainability-signal-plane/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Give each system one predictable address for its current energy and carbon figures.

## Context & Forces

Sustainability data is mostly written for people.

## Structure

The Internet-Draft "The 'sustainability-data' Well-Known URI" (Andrei N. Besleaga, 2026) defines /.well-known/sustainability-data, one JSON document over HTTPS.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Figures are self-declared: the format can be checked, the truth cannot.

## Related Patterns

- Goal Setting and Monitoring
```

## Goal Setting and Monitoring
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/goal-setting-and-monitoring/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Give an agent a goal with checkable criteria, then watch progress and correct course.

## Context & Forces

An agent can do every step right and still miss the goal.

## Structure

The classic form is the MAPE-K loop: Monitor, Analyze, Plan, Execute, over shared Knowledge.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Progress becomes visible, but criteria can replace the goal, so keep them few.

## Related Patterns

- Specification Gaming
- Metacognitive Monitoring and Control
- Unbounded Loops
- Termination and Exit Conditions
```

## Generative Agents
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/generative-agents/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Give a simulated character memory, reflection and plans, so it behaves consistently over days.

## Context & Forces

The whole history does not fit in a prompt.

## Structure

Park et al. (2023) describe a memory stream, reflection that turns memories into higher-level thoughts, and planning from retrieved memories.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Removing observation, planning or reflection each made behaviour less believable.

## Related Patterns

- Skill-Library Compounding
- Metacognitive Monitoring and Control
```

## Human-Only Merge Gate
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/human-only-merge-gate/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Keep agent-authored changes out of the main branch until a human merges them.

## Context & Forces

Prifti et al. (2026) note that self-review validates against the model that produced the output.

## Structure

GitHub's Copilot cloud agent pushes to a single branch and cannot approve or merge its pull requests; a human does.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

A human decides the merge, with the session log to review.

## Related Patterns

- Plan Approval Gate
- Tamper-Evident Agent Audit Log
```

## Plan Approval Gate
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/plan-approval-gate/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

The agent proposes a plan without editing source; a person approves it before edits start.

## Context & Forces

An agent that edits at once commits to an unseen approach.

## Structure

In Claude Code's plan mode, the agent explores and proposes changes without editing source until a person approves.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Reviewers judge the approach, not a large diff.

## Related Patterns

- The Autonomy Ladder
- Tamper-Evident Agent Audit Log
- Human-Only Merge Gate
```

## Agent Identity and Scoped Credentials
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/agent-identity-scoped-credentials/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Give each agent its own identity and short-lived, task-scoped credentials, so delegation never widens authority.

## Context & Forces

OWASP's ASI03 describes cached credentials reused across sessions and agents passing on their full access context.

## Structure

OWASP's ASI03 recommends "short-lived, narrowly scoped tokens per task" with per-agent identities.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Scoping needs precise task definitions, and an issuer must be available when tasks start.

## Related Patterns

- Tamper-Evident Agent Audit Log
- OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications
```

## Agentic Supply Chain Integrity
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/agentic-supply-chain/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Keep every component an agent loads traceable to a known source, unaltered, and revocable.

## Context & Forces

OWASP notes that agentic systems often compose capabilities at runtime, shifting focus from manifest to run-time security.

## Structure

OWASP's prevention list includes signing manifests, curated registries, rejecting unsigned components, re-checking signatures at runtime, and a kill switch.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

The sources describe controls, not measured results.

## Related Patterns

- OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications
- Skill-Library Compounding
```

## Dual-LLM Pattern
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/dual-llm-pattern/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Keep the acting model away from untrusted text, to limit what injected instructions can trigger.

## Context & Forces

E-mails and web pages can contain text that looks like a command.

## Structure

Simon Willison (2023) separates a privileged model with tools, a quarantined model reading untrusted content, and a controller.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

CaMeL (Debenedetti et al., 2025) solved 77% of AgentDojo tasks with provable security, against 84% undefended.

## Related Patterns

- OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications
- Memory and Context Poisoning Defense
```

## Memory and Context Poisoning Defense
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/memory-context-poisoning/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Treat every write to agent memory or a retrieval store as untrusted.

## Context & Forces

OWASP's ASI06, Memory & Context Poisoning, describes adversaries who corrupt or seed stored context.

## Structure

OWASP's mitigations include scanning new writes before commit, segmenting memory, requiring source attribution, and keeping snapshots for rollback.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

OWASP lists these mitigations without measuring them.

## Related Patterns

- Tamper-Evident Agent Audit Log
- Skill-Library Compounding
- OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications
```

## OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/owasp-agentic-top-10/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

One shared list of the security risks of software that acts on its own.

## The Categories

OWASP published this list on 9 December 2025, with ten entries from ASI01 Agent Goal Hijack to ASI10 Rogue Agents.

## How to Apply It

Check every agent capability against the ten entries and record a control or accepted risk.

## Related Patterns

- Dual-LLM Pattern
- Unbounded Loops
- Tamper-Evident Agent Audit Log
```

## Specification Gaming
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/specification-gaming/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Name a limit: an agent optimises the criterion you wrote, not the result you meant.

## Context & Forces

Every criterion simplifies intent.

## Structure

Krakovna et al. (2020) define specification gaming as behaviour that satisfies the literal specification of an objective without achieving the intended outcome.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Inspect traces when a metric jumps.

## Related Patterns

- Goal Setting and Monitoring
- Trajectory and Outcome Evaluation
- Weak-to-Strong Oversight
```

## Blackboard
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/blackboard/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Independent specialists work on one problem through a shared workspace, without calling each other.

## Context & Forces

Direct messages tie every agent to all the others.

## Structure

The Hearsay-II speech system (Erman et al., 1980) has a blackboard, independent knowledge sources and a control step.

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Knowledge sources interact through the blackboard alone, so their type and number can change.

## Related Patterns

- Parallelization
- Agents as Tools
```

## Multi-Agent Debate
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/multi-agent-debate/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Intent

Improve answers by having several model instances debate over rounds.

## Context & Forces

Du et al. (2023) have several language model instances debate and report fewer hallucinations.

## Structure

Liang et al. (2023) add affirmative and negative debaters and a judge to counter "Degeneration-of-Thought".

## Consequences & Trade-offs

Du et al. say the procedure is more computationally expensive, and that converged answers were not necessarily correct.

## Related Patterns

- Parallelization
- Blackboard
```

## Card format
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/card-format/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Specification

A card has an intent, the forces, the structure, the trade-offs and its related cards. Every claim names a public source. The text is about 60 words.
```

## Check a card against its sources
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/procedures/check-a-card-against-its-sources/ -->
```text agsc-content

# Check a card against its sources

## When

A card's sources were last checked more than six months ago.

## Steps

1. Open the card and read the `sources` in its header.
2. Open each source address.
3. Compare each sentence of the card with what the source says.
4. Propose the new `verified` date when they agree, or a corrected sentence when they do not.

## Checks

`agsc lint` passes on the proposal, and the proposal changes one card.
```

## Keep cards short
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/keep-cards-short/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Decision

Each card says one thing under each heading, in one sentence; two at most under Structure.
```

## Publish gate
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/gates/publish-gate/ -->
```text agsc-content

# Publish gate

Every change passes these checks, and a person merges it, before it is published.
```

## Re-check the sources of a card
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/task-recheck-sources/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Task

Pick one card. Open each of its sources and confirm it still says what the card says. Propose the new `verified` date, or a correction.
```

## Report a source that no longer answers
<!-- agsc:item https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/task-report-a-broken-link/ -->
```text agsc-content

## Task

Find a source address that no longer answers. Propose the working address, or report the card and the address.
```
